name: Fatty acid synthesis
summary: Liver, adipose and lactating breast in the fed state, in the cytosol. Acetyl-CoA leaves the mitochondria as citrate (citrate shuttle) and is released by ATP citrate lyase. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (rate-limiting, biotin) makes malonyl-CoA, which also blocks CPT I so new fat isn't burned. Fatty acid synthase builds palmitate (C16) from 1 acetyl-CoA + 7 malonyl-CoA using 14 NADPH (from the PPP and malic enzyme). Insulin turns it on; glucagon and epinephrine turn it off.

citrate.name: Citrate
citrate.notes: Made in the mitochondria (citrate synthase: acetyl-CoA + OAA) and exported by the citrate shuttle when ATP is high. Also allosterically activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

acetylcoa.name: Acetyl-CoA
acetylcoa.notes: Cytosolic acetyl-CoA; one molecule also primes fatty acid synthase.

oaa.name: Oxaloacetate
oaa.notes: Returns to the mitochondria as malate or pyruvate.

pyruvate.name: Pyruvate
pyruvate.notes: Re-enters the mitochondria, completing the shuttle.

malonylcoa.name: Malonyl-CoA
malonylcoa.notes: Committed intermediate. Inhibits CPT I, so fatty acid synthesis and β-oxidation don't run at once.

palmitate.name: Palmitate
palmitate.notes: Released by the thioesterase domain. Longer and unsaturated fatty acids are made in the ER; humans can't add double bonds past C9, so linoleic and α-linolenic acid are essential.

acl.name: ATP citrate lyase
acl.notes: Cleaves exported citrate back to acetyl-CoA + OAA in the cytosol. Induced by insulin.

mdh.name: Malate dehydrogenase
mdh.notes: Cytosolic isoform; shuttles OAA back toward the mitochondria.

me.name: Malic enzyme
me.notes: Makes NADPH for fatty acid synthase — the second NADPH source besides the pentose phosphate pathway.

acc.name: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase
acc.notes: Rate-limiting; needs biotin. Activated by insulin (dephosphorylation) and citrate; inhibited by glucagon/epinephrine (PKA), AMP-activated kinase (AMPK) and palmitoyl-CoA.

fas.name: Fatty acid synthase
fas.notes: One multifunctional homodimer with an acyl carrier protein (phosphopantetheine from pantothenic acid, B5). Seven cycles of condense–reduce–dehydrate–reduce, each using 2 NADPH and releasing CO₂.
